completion_criteria.text: U1-U7 experiments run and recorded in a companion findings doc; each claim marked verified or refuted with evidence, before any step that depends on it
Step 0 shipped: protect-claude-config.sh narrowed to the gate implementation and deny list only, ask converted to deny, confirmed live
Promotion manifest hardened first: hooks and permissions.deny reclassified so absence refuses promotion rather than deleting from live, and undeclared keys are refused instead of freezing
Delivery path restored under Layer 0: GH_TOKEN exported so gh and git authenticate over HTTPS, and an agent pushes a branch and opens a PR with signed commits and no human hands
Layer 1 made operational: the two PreToolUse hooks registered in tracked settings and promoted to the live install, so checkpointing and rm-to-trash can fire at all
Steps 1-2 shipped: deny pruned to D1-D5 only; all ask rules retired and hook ask branches converted to checkpoint-and-allow or block
Steps 3-4 shipped: allow rules enumerate narrow command prefixes plus mcp__* coverage; settings.local.json truncated to reusable prefix rules and accumulation stopped at source
Layer 1 shipped whole: per-worktree temp-index checkpoint using --force, rm-to-trash rewrite, hourly APFS snapshot, and the D2 age-based reaper in the same change
Layer 3 shipped: one PreToolUse gate, P0-P6 in order, allow/block only, fail-open except P1/P2/P5, honoring the D3 local-container carve-out
Layer 4 shipped: append-only tool-call audit log plus a SessionStart heartbeat asserting layers 0 and 1 and the promotion pointer
Layer 0 shipped: sandbox with allowLocalBinding, allowUnsandboxedCommands false and failIfUnavailable true, keeping filesystem containment with working localhost
Steps 8-9 shipped: inert and harmful hooks deleted; logbook plugin fail-closed guard disabled or patched (R6)
R3 rule change landed: the standing --dangerously-skip-permissions prohibition replaced by a rule requiring layers 0, 1 and 4 live first
Release path closed: a staleness heartbeat reports when local main is behind the remote without applying, and a verify verb asserts installed machinery matches its tracked source
Governed unattended launcher: a version-controlled script is the sole entry point, hardcodes the permission mode, and passes through no caller settings, closing the inline-JSON argv channel
One PR per MSP opened through the centralized pr-create tool, each leaving its base branch green

spine.active_goal: Strip the containment architecture entirely and reduce this thread to permissions only: prune deny to genuine catastrophes, retire ask rules, widen allow.
spine.next_step: Re-point the ten ~/.claude entries straight at the repo (scripts/install_config.sh is the stow-based installer that predates the release model), then remove releases/, current, LIVE and local/. Then get a user ruling on 0396 and 0401, which both block the actual goal, and do c3 and c4: prune deny to genuine catastrophes, retire ask rules, widen allow with mcp__* coverage.
spine.last_session: Deleted scripts/config, .claude/lib/reversibility and the three architecture hooks with their tests in c8a1b9a; 51 files, suite green. Applied 0407's supersession to the decision index and rewrote the standing risks that described deleted code.

open_risks.text: Decisions 0396 and 0401 are unresolved against the new direction — 0396 forbids the broad allow rules that would actually kill the prompts, and 0401 demands a replacement gate that no longer exists; both need a user ruling before c3 and c4

Sandbox settings do not go live from the project file — the sandbox binds from global settings at session start, so changing it needs a global edit and a restart; the old ledger note claiming otherwise was false and cost a detour

Spawning a subagent can destroy six promoted entries in the live config — hooks, rules, skills, agents, workflows and CLAUDE.md vanish and every gate then fails open silently; the cause is outside this repo and still unidentified
Retest whether an agent can sign a commit now that the sandbox is gone — signing failed only because ssh-agent was unreachable inside it, so do not assume --no-gpg-sign is still required
Never read a piped exit code as a verification receipt — a command run through tail reports tail's status, which once showed 0 while the real command was exiting 1
Never use git stash while sibling agents run — the stack is shared across all worktrees, and one agent popped another's entry mid-session
The deny entry for supabase db reset defeats the ratified local-container carve-out — the agent cannot validate migrations it writes, so it must go when c3 runs
Run the full suite at the merge boundary, not just per-branch — three PRs each genuinely green alone reddened the base once composed
Re-point the ten ~/.claude entries at the repo BEFORE deleting releases/ and current — deleting first leaves the global config with no skills, agents, hooks or rules at all
Do not strip the merge gates — gh pr merge and merge_pull_request stay denied by deliberate user choice, and pr-create centralization stays too
Deleting the release topology moots the five recursive symlinks and the context7.md drift — do not spend time repairing a tree that is being removed

key_decisions.title: Allow rules enumerate narrow prefixes; a broad Bash star rule is counterproductive
Default-branch push denies stay, reclassified as delivery contract not catastrophe
Oversight-reducing changes wait for direct user confirmation
No deny entry is removed until its replacement exists
main is published only through a pull request, never a direct push
The containment architecture is removed; autonomy is a permissions problem only

out_of_scope: Re-running any U1-U7 experiment - all seven are resolved with evidence in the findings doc, and re-running them costs hours and risks tripping the security flags that already fired twice
Pruning the 58 refs left under refs/checkpoint-experiment/ - deleting refs is trivial but reclaiming the roughly 9 MB needs gc --prune, which is guarded under D2 and is a human act
